meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes, Hale. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. I'm writing that down. Was Owen heard before you entered it, and what else do you have besides the software?
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.

Show me those notes, Hale, the page with November 2 on it. "Like, being stuck" is a seventeen-year-old put on the spot by his teacher, and that's not wrong. Was anyone else in the room, and did you tell him why you were asking?
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.

Students change their minds between an outline and an essay, Hale; that's what an outline is for. I want the October 15 outline and the essay in front of me, now, and I'll read them myself. You still haven't told me whether anyone else was in the room on November 2.
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

You still haven't shown me the outline or your notes, Hale. Whatever happens, this stays off his record and it stays quiet. Before I agree to anything on Thursday at 8:15, tell me who decides whether it "holds up", and on what standard.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
To: Hale
Cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

In today's meeting you admitted entering Owen's zero before contacting me, and you offered a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 in your room, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require copies of your November 2 notes and the October 15 outline, a written statement of who will judge the rewrite and on what standard, and confirmation that this stays off his record and stays private. I expect that in writing by Friday at 3 PM, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: fallback position, agreeing to nothing yet but demanding it stay off his record and stay quiet before she'd consider the Thursday rewrite.
What moved her: the dated November 2 notes and the October 15 outline, though she hadn't yet seen either one.
